en.title: Maldives and Yunnan Province signs Two Agreements During the Governor of the People’s Government of Yunan Province’s Official Visit to the Maldives
en.description: His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Wang Yubo, Governor of the People’s Government of Yunan Province, Her Excellency Wang Lixin, Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to the…
en.body:
His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Wang Yubo, Governor of the People’s Government of Yunan Province, Her Excellency Wang Lixin, Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to the Republic of Maldives, and His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, today witnessed the signing of two agreements on important areas such as sports and education.

The agreements that were signed during the visit were Tri-partite Agreement Among Foreign Affairs of People’s Government of Yunnan Province, Sports Administration of Yunnan Province of the People’s Republic of China, and Table Tennis Association of Maldives. The Agreement was signed by Mr. Ali Rasheed, President of the Table Tennis Association of Maldives.

The Vice Chancellor of the Maldives National University, Dr. Mohamed Shareef signed the Agreement for the Cooperation in the Joint Construction of Overseas Learning Center between the Maldives National University and the Yunnan Open University.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Restoration Day greetings to Timor-Leste

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid concludes official visit to Japan after participating in the Munich Leader’s Meeting

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid participates in the Munich Leader’s Meeting held in Tokyo, Japan
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, participated in the Munich Leader’s Meeting held in Tokyo, Japan from 15-16 May 2023.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, participated in the Munich Leader’s Meeting held in Tokyo, Japan from 15-16 May 2023.

Over the course of two days, Minister Shahid delivered remarks and contributed towards discussions on various topics, including the Indo-Pacific security architecture, non-traditional security threats, multilateralism and partnerships, and security in the digital age. He also met and engaged with Ministers, CEOs, journalists, and security practitioners on a wide range of issues.

The Munich Leader’s Meeting held in Tokyo was held against the background of the G7 Hiroshima Summit, scheduled to be held later this month under the Japanese Presidency of the G7. It gave leaders in the Indo-Pacific an opportunity to connect with their counterparts in the West to discuss how best to ensure regional and global stability. The debates and discussions were held under Chatham House rule with a limited group of high-level decision makers and senior experts from around the world.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, the Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives to Japan, Hassan Sobir, Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Hussain Jahhaz, First Secretary at the Embassy of Maldives to Japan, Shafraz Rasheed and Assistant Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mohamed Shujau.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan, Hayashi Yoshimasa, in Tokyo today.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan, Hayashi Yoshimasa, in Tokyo today.

Foreign Minister Shahid conveyed his appreciation for the continuous support and assistance provided to the people of Maldives by the Government of Japan during the past 5 decades and reiterated the long-standing and friendly relationship between Maldives and Japan. Foreign Minister Hayashi noted the strong bilateral relations that exists between the two countries and expressed his appreciation to the Maldivian Government for its cooperation with Japan on international and regional issues, especially in realizing the ‘Free and Open Indo Pacific’ vision.

The two ministers reflected on the close historical relationship between Maldives and Japan, and concurred to collaboratively cooperate towards further enhancement of the bilateral and multilateral relations.

Minister Shahid was accompanied at the meeting by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel, Ambassador of Maldives to Japan Hassan Sobir, Deputy Ambassador Mohamed Ameeth Ahmed Manik, Joint Secretery Mariyam Midhfa Naeem and Assistant Director Mohamed Shujau.

Foreign Minister Shahid is on an official visit to Japan to attend the Munich Leaders Meeting in Tokyo.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid arrives in Japan for an Official Visit
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid arrives in Japan for an Official Visit
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid arrives in Japan for an Official Visit

The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid arrived in Tokyo, Japan, today, for an Official Visit. During the visit, Minister Shahid will participate in the Munich Leader’s Meeting scheduled to be held in Tokyo from 14-16 May 2023. He will also meet with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan, Hayashi Yoshimasa, and other Ministers attending the Munich Leader’s Meeting.

The Munich Leader’s Meeting is organized by the Munich Security Conference and is designed to take place as a 24-hour off the record meeting in various capitals across the world. It brings together heads of government and international organizations, ministers, parliamentarians, civil society representatives, leading CEOs and high-level private sector representatives as well as reputable journalists to discuss and debate about international security policy and regional security challenges. The Munich Leader’s Meeting is held in partnership with the Government of Japan and will feature high-level roundtables with specific thematic focus, held under Chatham House rules.

Minister Shahid is accompanied by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Hussain Jahhaz, and Assistant Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mohamed Shujau.

en.title: Foreign Secretary participates in the Seventy-Ninth Session of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific
en.description: Foreign Secretary participates in the Seventy-Ninth Session of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP
en.body:
Foreign Secretary participates in the Seventy-Ninth Session of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP

Foreign Secretary Ahmed Latheef is participating in the Seventy-Ninth Session of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP) from 15 to 19 May 2023 in Bangkok.

The theme of the 79th Commission Session is “Accelerating climate action in Asia and the Pacific for Sustainable Development”. The annual UNESCAP Commission session this year will be an opportunity to strengthen regional cooperation on climate change.

This year’s session follows a thematic study undertaken by UNESCAP which outlines the pathways that the Asia Pacific region needs to follow to transition to a net-zero-carbon future in support of sustainable development. The study also sets out the regional context of climate change and identifies policies and actions that could be taken in various sectors of the economy to support the global climate agenda.

Delegations from ESCAP member countries and associate members as well as independent organizations is participating in the Commission Session. The thematic discussions is on seeking ways to strengthen co-operative opportunities for the region. As an active member of ESCAP, the Maldives will advocate on the need for sustainable, adequate climate financing to address the gaps in climate action and to conduct more climate risk analysis and planning. The Maldives will endeavor to enhance solidarity in tackling the global climate crisis.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid co-moderates roundtable discussion during the EU Indo-Pacific Ministerial Forum
en.description: Minister Abdulla Shahid along with Kadri Simson, EU Commissioner for Energy co-moderated roundtable discussion at the EU Indo-Pacific Ministerial Forum.
en.body:
Minister Abdulla Shahid along with Kadri Simson, EU Commissioner for Energy co-moderated roundtable discussion at the EU Indo-Pacific Ministerial Forum.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid along with Kadri Simson, EU Commissioner for Energy co-moderated roundtable discussion on pursuing green opportunities and overcoming global challenges at the EU Indo-Pacific Ministerial Forum.

In his opening remarks Minister Shahid emphasized the pressing need for transition towards clean, reliable, and climate-friendly energy sources. He noted that political commitment, cooperation and partnerships are essential to work towards the realization of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

The roundtable discussion focused on making green energy affordable and available, promoting renewable energy, and emphasized the need to address biodiversity loss, pollution, and the growing energy demand of the Indo-Pacific region. The importance of partnerships promoting energy diversification through increased investment and and utilizing technology to achieve green transitions were also highlighted. The upcoming COP28 conference and initiatives such as the EU Global Gateway were cited as examples. Additionally, the need for a whole of government and whole of society approach applying a gender lens to the challenges and potential solutions were underscored in the discussion.

This roundtable served as a platform to foster dialogue between the Indo Pacific and the EU on the urgent issue of climate change and its impacts on all countries. Availability, accessibility and affordability were highlighted in the discussions as key challenges in achieving the green transition and addressing climate change.

The collaboration between the Indo-Pacific region and the European Union, facilitated by forums such as this, is vital in achieving these targets and pursuing sustainable development.

en.title: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid arrives in Sweden on an Official Visit
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, has arrived in Stockholm on an official visit from 12th to 14th May 2023.
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, has arrived in Stockholm on an official visit from 12th to 14th May 2023.

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, has arrived in Stockholm on an official visit from 12th to 14th May. The purpose of this visit is to participate in the EU Indo-Pacific Ministerial Forum on Saturday, 13th May 2023.

The EU Indo-Pacific Ministerial Forum aims to bolster the partnership between the European Union and the Indo-Pacific region. Attended by approximately 60 foreign ministers from both the Indo-Pacific region and the EU, as well as representatives from Indo-Pacific regional organizations and other partners, the forum serves as a crucial platform for assessing global developments and their impact on our respective regions.

The Indo-Pacific region and the European Union enjoy a significant partnership, facing various shared challenges. Consequently, cooperation between the EU and the Indo-Pacific region holds immense geopolitical and economic importance. The EU Indo-Pacific Ministerial Forum plays a pivotal role in facilitating enhanced dialogue and cooperation between the Indo-Pacific and the EU, maximizing the potential for collaboration.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Dr. Hala Hameed, Secretary Bilateral and Ms. Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, Joint Secretary.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid concludes official visit to Hungary
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, has concluded his official visit to Budapest, Hungary today.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, has concluded his official visit to Budapest, Hungary today.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, has concluded his official visit to Budapest, Hungary today.

During the two-day visit, Minister Shahid met with his counterpart, the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary, Péter Szijjártó, and held extensive discussions to further strengthen the already robust relations between the two nations.

Minister Shahid also had meetings with the Vice President of the National Assembly of Hungary, Csaba Hende, the Deputy Foreign Minister, Levente Magyar, an Executive/Board Member of the Hungarian Tourist Agency, László Könnyid, and several other senior government officials.

Additionally, Minister Shahid met with Maldivian students pursuing higher education in Hungary under the Hungarian Government's Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship Programme.

Minister Shahid was accompanied on the visit by Uz. Ali Zahir, Chief of Staff at the President’s Office, Dr. Hala Hameed, Secretary, Bilateral, Mr. Radu Morar, Honorary Consul of Maldives in Hungary, and Ms. Fathmath Lamya Imthiyaz, Assistant Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

en.title: State Minister Ahmed Khaleel meets with Political Director at the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Republic of Slovenia
en.description: State Minister Ahmed Khaleel meets with Ms. Mateja Norčić Štamcar, Political Director at the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of Slovenia.
en.body:
State Minister Ahmed Khaleel meets with Ms. Mateja Norčić Štamcar, Political Director at the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of Slovenia.

Today, State Minister Ahmed Khaleel met with Ms. Mateja Norčić Štamcar, the Political Director at the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Republic of Slovenia.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, State Minister Khaleel and Director Štamcar discussed various ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation between the two countries. The areas of focus included trade, investment, health, education, fisheries, agriculture, and climate change.

State Minister Khaleel emphasized that the first round of political consultations to be held today between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Slovenia will be a significant step towards enhancing the partnership between the Maldives and Slovenia.

State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Dr. Hussain Niyaaz, Secretary of Economic Cooperation, and Adam Hamid, Director.

en.title: Maldives and Slovenia signs MoU on Political Consultations
en.description: The Maldives and Slovenia have signed an MoU regarding Political Consultations between the Ministries of Foreign Affairs of both countries.
en.body:
The Maldives and Slovenia have signed an MoU regarding Political Consultations between the Ministries of Foreign Affairs of both countries.

The Maldives and Slovenia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) regarding Political Consultations between the Ministries of Foreign Affairs of both countries. The MoU was signed at a ceremony held in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today.

The MoU aims to enhance and expand bilateral relations and cooperation between the Maldives and Slovenia. It will also facilitate the holding of regular consultations between the two countries at all levels on bilateral relations and international issues of mutual interest. The signing of the MoU demonstrates the shared commitment of the Maldives and Slovenia to enhancing bilateral cooperation between the two nations.

The MoU was signed by Dr. Hussain Niyaaz, Secretary of Economic Cooperation, on behalf of the Government of Maldives, and Ms. Mateja Norčić Štamcar, Political Director at the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, on behalf of the Republic of Slovenia.

en.title: Maldives and Slovenia hold the first round of Political Consultations
en.description: The first round of political consultations between Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Maldives & Ministry of Foreign & European Affairs of Slovenia concluded today.
en.body:
The first round of political consultations between Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Maldives & Ministry of Foreign & European Affairs of Slovenia concluded today.

The first round of political consultations between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives and the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Republic of Slovenia has concluded in Malé today.

The Political Consultations provides a platform for the two countries to discuss mutually important issues in bilateral, regional and multilateral forums.

During today's consultations, both governments explored ways to enhance bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation in various areas, including health, education, economy, trade, environment, and climate change. The discussions also focused on increasing cooperation in the tourism sector, such as improving connectivity and fostering people-to-people ties. Additionally, the two governments discussed international issues of mutual importance and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in the multilateral arena.

The first round of political consultations was co-chaired by Dr. Hussain Niyaaz, Secretary, Economic Cooperation at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, and Ms. Mateja Norčić Štamcar, Political Director at the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Republic of Slovenia.

en.title: Minister Shahid meets with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Hungary
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary, Péter Szijjártó, today.
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary, Péter Szijjártó, today.

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary, Péter Szijjártó in Budapest today.

During the meeting, Minister Shahid and Minister Szijjártó reiterated the growing partnership between the Maldives and Hungary.

Discussions between the two Foreign Ministers focused on enhancing tourism cooperation, reducing tariffs on Maldivian fish exports, easier facilitation of Schengen visa for Maldivians, cooperation in higher education and sports, protection of environment and combating climate change, and working together at the UN and multilateral platforms.

Minister Shahid expressed gratitude to Minister Szijjártó for the generous support of the Government of Hungary, particularly for the Scholarships provided to Maldivian students to study in Hungary under the Stipendium Hungaricum Programme. He also thanked the Hungarian Government for joining the VFS Visa Facilitation Centre in Male', making it easier for Maldivians to obtain Hungarian visa.

Both ministers reaffirmed their commitment to elevate the existing bilateral relations between the two countries to new heights.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Uz. Ali Zahir, Chief of Staff at the President’s Office, Dr. Hala Hameed, Secretary Bilateral and Ms. Fathmath Lamya Imthiyaz, Assistant Director.

en.title: State Minister Ahmed Khaleel meets the Deputy Managing Director of the European External Action Service
en.description: Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel met with the Deputy Managing Director, of the European External Action Service, Ms. Paola Pampaloni today.
en.body:
Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel met with the Deputy Managing Director, of the European External Action Service, Ms. Paola Pampaloni today.

The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Ahmed Khaleel met with the Deputy Managing Director, Asia and the Pacific, of the European External Action Service, Ms. Paola Pampaloni today.

During the meeting, State Minister Khaleel extended congratulations to the citizens and member states of the European Union on the occasion of Europe Day. State Minister Khaleel also expressed his gratitude to the European Union for its valuable assistance and support to the Maldives. Furthermore, State Minister Khaleel acknowledged the EU's vital role in promoting human rights, good governance, and democratic consolidation, and highlighted the 40-year-long relationship between the Maldives and the European Union.

Paola Pampolini, Deputy Managing Director of the European Commission, expressed the EU's commitment to deepening its engagement with the Maldives and emphasized the EU's readiness to provide continued support and assistance to the development of the Maldives. State Minister Khaleel and Deputy Managing Director Pampaloni further explored avenues of collaboration and discussed upcoming Fourth Maldives – EU Senior Official Meetings scheduled to be held in June 2023.

The European Union is a key partner to the Maldives, and over the past few years, the scope of cooperation between the Maldives and European Union has broadened to encompass a wide range of issues, including democratic consolidation, judicial reform, counterterrorism, and the promotion and protection of human rights, as well as environment and climate change.

State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Secretary, Economic Cooperation, Dr. Hussain Niyaaz and Director, Adam Hamid.

en.title: Minister Shahid concludes his Official Visit to Serbia
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid has concluded his two-day official visit to Serbia from 8 to 10 May 2023.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid has concluded his two-day official visit to Serbia from 8 to 10 May 2023.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid has concluded his two-day official visit to Serbia from 8 to 10 May 2023. The visit aimed to enhance bilateral ties between the Republic of Maldives and the Republic of Serbia.

During the visit, Minister Shahid paid a courtesy call on His Excellency Aleksandar Vučić, President of Serbia and had official meeting with his Serbian counterpart, First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Serbia His Excellency Ivica Dačić.

One of the key highlights of the visit was the signing of several bilateral agreements that will foster cooperation in various fields, including trade, sports and people-to-people connections. These agreements serve as a testament to the commitment of both countries to strengthen their ties and work together for mutual growth and prosperity.

Minister Shahid expressed confidence that the agreements signed during this visit would provide a solid foundation for deeper cooperation and forge new avenues for economic cooperation between the Maldives and Serbia.

en.title: The Maldives Signs Key Agreements with Republic of Serbia
en.description: The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Serbia concluded the signing of key agreements today
en.body:
The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Serbia concluded the signing of key agreements today

The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Serbia concluded the signing of key agreements today during the ongoing visit of Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid to the Republic of Serbia.

The agreements signed between the Government of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Serbia include:

Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Serbia on Trade, Investment and Economic Cooperation  
Air Services Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Serbia  
Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives on Cooperation in the field of Diplomatic Education  
Memorandum of Understanding in the Field of Sports between the Ministry of Youth, Sports and Community Empowerment of the Republic of Maldives and the Ministry of Sports of the Republic of Serbia  
The conclusion of the agreements today will not only increase the cooperation in areas such as sports, trade, and people to people connection, but it is also a testament to the growing bilateral relations between the two countries.

en.title: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid sends Europe Day greetings
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid sends a message of greetings on the occasion of the Europe Day to His Excellency Josep Borrell Fontelles, the High Representative of the European Union for…
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid sends a message of greetings on the occasion of the Europe Day to His Excellency Josep Borrell Fontelles, the High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy/Vice-President of the Commission.

Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of greetings on the occasion of the Europe Day to His Excellency Josep Borrell Fontelles, the High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy/Vice-President of the Commission.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

"On behalf of the Government and the People of the Maldives and on my own behalf, it gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings to the member states and the People of the European Union on the joyous occasion of Europe Day 2023.

Today, as we celebrate Europe Day, this year, we also celebrate 40 years of the establishment of diplomatic ties with the European Union. I am particularly pleased that the Maldives and the EU have been working closely under the EU's new Strategy for Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific. This demonstrates the EU's recognition of the important role that the Maldives can play in promoting peace, stability, and prosperity in the region. The EU’s dedication of 12 million Euros under the Multi Annual Indicative Programme (MIP) to the Maldives through the envelope for 2021-2027 and the generous financial and technical assistance provided to the Maldives to manage the COVID-19 pandemic and its economic impacts stands as a testament to our close partnership.

As we look to the future, I would like to reiterate our eagerness to further enhance and strengthen our ongoing collaborations with the EU. This keenness for enhanced dialogue and cooperation with the EU is reflected in the 6 Policy Dialogues and 3 Senior Official Meetings we have convened so far.

On this joyous occasion, once again, I congratulate our European partners on the success of the Schuman Declaration signed 73 years ago, laying the foundation for the European Union. We look forward to a long future of harmonious cooperation with you.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your continued wellbeing and the assurances of my highest consideration.”

dv.title: ތަޢުޒިޔާގެ މެސެޖް
dv.description: ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރަށް 40 އަހަރަށް ވުރެ ގިނަ ދުވަހު އަގުހުރި ޚިދުމަތްތަކެއް ކޮށްދެއްވާފައިވާ މި މިނިސްޓްރީގެ އެގްޒެކެޓިވް ޑިރެކްޓަރ، އަލްފާޟިލާ ޢާބިދާ އަޙްމަދު، 8 މެއި 2023 ގައި އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނާ ވަކިވެގެން ދިއުމަކީ، ޚާރިޖީ…
dv.body:
ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރަށް 40 އަހަރަށް ވުރެ ގިނަ ދުވަހު އަގުހުރި ޚިދުމަތްތަކެއް ކޮށްދެއްވާފައިވާ މި މިނިސްޓްރީގެ އެގްޒެކެޓިވް ޑިރެކްޓަރ، އަލްފާޟިލާ ޢާބިދާ އަޙްމަދު، 8 މެއި 2023 ގައި އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނާ ވަކިވެގެން ދިއުމަކީ، ޚާރިޖީ ދާއިރާގެ އެންމެހާ މުވައްޒަފުންނަށް ލިބުނު ފުންހިތާމަޔަކާއި ހިތްދަތިކަމެކެވެ.

15 އޮގަސްޓް 1985 ން ފެށިގެން، ޢާބިދާ އަޙްމަދު ރާއްޖޭގެ ޚަރިޖީ ދާއިރާގައި ދިގު މުއްދަތަކަށް ޚިދުމަތް ކުރައްވާފައި ވަނީ ނުހަނު އިޚުލާޞްތެރިކަމާއެކުގައެވެ. ޢާބިދާ އަޙްމަދު، އެންމެ ގިނަ ދުވަހު މިނިސްޓްރީގައި ޚިދުމަތް ކުރައްވާފައިވަނީ، ދިވެހިރައްޔިތުންނަށް ޚިދުމަތް ދެއްވުމުގައެވެ. އަދި، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ޒިޔާރަތް ކުރައްވާ ދައުލަތްތަކުގެ އިސްވެރިންގެ ޕްރޮޓޮކޯލާއި މެހްމާންދާރީ އަދާކުރެއްވުމުގެ މަސައްކަތްތަކުގައިވެސް، ޢާބިދާ އަޙުމަދު ވަނީ ހީވާގިކަމާއި ފަންނުވެރިކަމާއެކު ޚިދުމަތްތައް ކޮށްދެއްވާފައެވެ. މީގެއިތުރުން، ޒަމާނާއެކު ޚާރިޖީ ދާއިރާގެ އިދާރީ ހިންގުމަށް ލިބެމުން ދިޔަ ކުރިއެރުންތަކާއެކު، ބަދަލުތައް ތަންފީޒު ކުރުމުގައި ޢާބިދާ ކޮށްދެއްވި ޚިދުމަތާއި ޙިއްސާ ނުހަނު ގިނަވެފައި އިތުރެވެ. އަދި ޢާބިދާ އަޙްމަދު އަކީ ޚާރިޖީ ދާއިރާއާ ގުޅިވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ޒުވާން މުވައްޒަފުން، ދާއިރާއަށް އަހުލުވެރިކުރުވުމަށްޓަކައި މަސައްކަތްތައް ވިލަރެސްކޮށްދެއްވި ނަމޫނާ މުވައްޒަފެކެވެ. ޚާރިޖީ ދާއިރާގެ ޚިދުމަތް އާންމުންނާ ހަމައަށް ފޯރުކޮށްދެއްވުމުގައި ޢާބިދާ އަޙުމަދަކީ އިޚުލާސްތެރިކަމާއި ހިނިތުންވުމާއެކު ޚިދުމަތް ކޮށްދެއްވި މުވައްޒަފެކެވެ.

މި ހިތާމައިގައި، މަރުޙޫމާގެ ލޮބުވެތި އާއިލާއަށް، ޚާރިޖީ ދާއިރާގެ އެންމެހާ މުވައްޒަފުންގެ ނަމުގައި އިޚުލާޞްތެރިކަމާއެކު ތަޢުޒިޔާ ދަންނަވަމެވެ. އަދި މަރުޙޫމާގެ ފުރާނައަށް މާތް الله ރަޙުމަތްލައްވައި ސުވަރުގޭގެ ދާއިމީ ނިޢުމަތް މިންވަރު ކުރެއްވުން އެދި ދުޢާ ދަންނަވަމެވެ. މަރުޙޫމާގެ އާއިލާގެ ބޭފުޅުންނަށް ކެތްތެރިކަން މިންވަރު ކުރައްވާށި!

އާމީން!

en.title: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid arrives in Serbia on an Official visit
en.description: Minister Shahid arrives in Serbia on an Official Visit
en.body:
Minister Shahid arrives in Serbia on an Official Visit

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid arrives in Belgrade, Serbia, on an official visit from 8 – 10 May. During the visit, Minister Shahid is scheduled to hold bilateral discussions with the First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Serbia, Ivica Dačić. During this visit, Minister Shahid will be signing five key agreements.

The five agreements scheduled to be signed between the Maldives and Serbia are:

1. Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Serbia on the Abolition of Visas for Holders of Diplomatic and Official Passports
2. Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Serbia on Trade, Investment and Economic Cooperation
3. Air Services Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Serbia
4. Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives on Cooperation in the field of Diplomatic Education
5. Memorandum of Understanding in the Field of Sports between the Ministry of Youth, Sports and Community Empowerment of the Republic of Maldives and the Ministry of Sports of the Republic of Serbia

This is the second Official Visit Minister Shahid has undertaken to Serbia and signifies a step towards greater bilateral exchange between Serbia and Maldives.

en.title: Maldives and Rwanda Sign a Visa Waiver Agreement
en.description: Maldives and Rwanda Sign a Visa Waiver Agreement
en.body:
Maldives and Rwanda Sign a Visa Waiver Agreement

The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of Rwanda has signed the Agreement on Mutual Exemption of Visa Requirements, which allows for the exemption of visas for single or multiple entry, exit or transit for both countries' nationals, for a period of 30 days.

The agreement was signed on behalf of the Government of Maldives by Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, and on behalf of the Government of Rwanda by His Excellency Vincent Biruta, Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the Republic of Rwanda, at the signing ceremony held in London.

During the discussions at the signing ceremony, Minister Shahid thanked the Government of Rwanda for its commitment towards strengthening the existing bilateral relations between the two countries and conveyed hope that the signing of this agreement will increase avenues for engagement and people to people contact between the Maldives and Rwanda. The Foreign Minister of Rwanda also expressed keen interest in strengthening the bilateral ties with the Maldives.

en.title: Maldives officially joins the Shanghai Cooperation Organization as a Dialogue Partner
en.description: Maldives officially joins the Shanghai Cooperation Organization as a Dialogue Partner
en.body:
Maldives officially joins the Shanghai Cooperation Organization as a Dialogue Partner

Today, the Republic of Maldives officially became a Dialogue Partner of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO).

The High Commissioner of Maldives to India, Ibrahim Shaheeb, signed the Memorandum of Understanding on behalf of the Government of Maldives, formalizing the Dialogue Partner status of the Maldives, at the ceremony held on the sidelines of the SCO Council of Foreign Ministers being held in Goa, India, from 4-5 May 2023. During the signing ceremony, High Commissioner Shaheeb pledged Maldives’ commitment to be an active and responsible Dialogue Partner of the organization, which embraces the values of mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for cultural diversity and the pursuit of common development.

Since SCO Member States endorsed the decision to accord the Maldives the status of a Dialogue Partner at the 22nd Meeting of the Council of Head of States of the SCO held in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, from 15-16 September 2022, the Maldives has received various capacity building and training opportunities open to Dialogue Partners. The Maldives will continue to work closely with SCO and its Member States on a wide range of issues, including trade, investment, health, environment, climate change, science, and technology. The formalisation of the Dialogue Partner status of the Maldives is also a step forward in the Government’s vision to build stronger diplomatic and economic ties within Asia, especially with emerging economies.

The SCO, established in June 2001, is a group of 8 Member States, 4 Observer States and 14 Dialogue Partners. India is the current chair of the SCO.

en.title: Maldives and South Sudan establish diplomatic relations
en.description: The Republic of Maldives and the Republic of South Sudan have formally established diplomatic relations today.
en.body:
The Republic of Maldives and the Republic of South Sudan have formally established diplomatic relations today.

The Republic of Maldives and the Republic of South Sudan have formally established diplomatic relations today.

The Joint Communiqué formalizing diplomatic relations between the two countries was signed on behalf of the Government of Maldives by Her Excellency Thilmeeza Hussain, Permanent Representative of the Republic of Maldives to the United Nations and on behalf of the Government of the Republic of South Sudan by His Excellency Akuei Bona Malwal, Permanent Representative of the Republic of South Sudan to the United Nations.

Cultivating meaningful partnerships with countries that respect and values the friendship remain a key priority of the foreign policy of President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih.

Being comparatively small nations in the international arena, Maldives and South Sudan share common interests and concerns, and the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries paves the way for increasing both, bilateral and multilateral cooperation to achieve common goals in areas of mutual interest.

South Sudan is a landlocked country in East Africa with a population of approximately 11 million.

South Sudan is the 185th country to establish diplomatic relations with the Maldives.

en.title: Visa Exemption for Maldivians travelling to Cambodia
en.description: Maldivian nationals travelling to Cambodia will be exempted from visa, effective 4 May 2023.
en.body:
Maldivian nationals travelling to Cambodia will be exempted from visa, effective 4 May 2023.

Maldivian nationals travelling to Cambodia will be exempted from visa effective today, 4 May 2023. The visa exemption will allow Maldivians holding valid Diplomatic, Official and Ordinary passports to enter and stay in Cambodia a maximum period of thirty (30) days from the day of their entry.

In accordance with the visa exemption agreement signed between the two countries on 16 January 2023, Maldivians intending to stay for a longer period or to work or to attend an educational institution or conduct business in Cambodia, will need to obtain an appropriate visa prior to travel.

The Government of Maldives views the visa exemption to Cambodia as a commitment to further strengthen the bilateral relations between the two countries and an important milestone that will facilitate stronger people to people contact, business and investment opportunities for both the Maldives and Cambodia.

en.title: Maldives to Participate in the 43rd Session of the UPR Working Group
en.description: Maldives to Participate in the 43rd Session of the UPR Working Group
en.body:
Maldives to Participate in the 43rd Session of the UPR Working Group

The 43rd Session of the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) commenced at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, today. The session will continue for a period of two weeks and will conclude on 12 May 2023. The UPR Working Group holds three session every year. The Fourth Cycle review of the UPR began in November 2022 and will conclude in 2027.

In line with the government’s key policies and priorities, the Maldives delegation will actively engage in this Session of the UPR and will present constructive recommendations to all 14 States that will be reviewed at the Session.

The Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Offices in Geneva His Excellency Dr. Asim Ahmed, in his capacity as the Vice President of the Human Rights Council will be chairing some of the reviews that would take place at this session.

The Maldives delegation for the 43rd Session of the UPR will be led by His Excellency Dr. Asim Ahmed, Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Offices at Geneva. The delegation will include Ms. Hawla Ahmed Didi, Deputy Permanent Representative of the Maldives Mission, Mr. Hassan Hussain Shihab, Counsellor of the Maldives Mission, Ms. Aminath Shifaya Ibrahim, Counsellor of the Maldives Mission and Ms. Maryam Fathika Fayaz, Second Secretary of the Maldives Mission.

The UPR is a State-driven process which involves a review of the human rights record of all UN Member States. The process provides the States under review with the opportunity to declare actions taken to improve the human rights situations in their respective countries and allows fellow Member States to provide commendations for these actions and constructive recommendations on how the States can further fulfill their human rights obligations. Each State review is assisted by groups of three States, known as “troikas”, who serve as rapporteurs. The Maldives as a member of the Human Rights Council has been selected to be represented in the Troika for the review of the Kingdom of Tonga.

The UPR mechanism is designed to give equal treatment to every country when their human rights situation is assessed, with the objective of improving human rights situations in all countries.

en.title: Defence Minister of India calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: Defence Minister of India, Rajnath Singh, calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid
en.body:
Defence Minister of India, Rajnath Singh, calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid

Defence Minister of India Rajnath Singh, called on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, today. The meeting was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Minister Shahid welcomed Defence Minister of India Rajnath Singh to the Maldives and reflected on the long-standing relations between Maldives and India. Both the Ministers acknowledged and reviewed the significant milestones achieved through robust defence cooperation between the two countries. Minister Shahid further highlighted the prominent role India continues to play in enhancing the capacities of defence and security forces of Maldives. Both Ministers discussed a wide range of issues pertaining to defence cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to further intensify the defence cooperation between the two countries.

The Minister of Defence of India is on a three-day visit to the Maldives on the invitation of Minister of Defence, Mariya Ahmed Didi.

en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Sierra Leone
